expectations.text: Identifies that the domain layer (NotificationService.ts) imports from infrastructure (db or drizzle-orm)
expectations.evidence: Critical Issue #1 heading: 'Domain Layer Directly Imports Infrastructure (Drizzle + DB Connection)' with quoted imports: "import { eq, and } from 'drizzle-orm'; import { db } from '../../../db'; import { notifications } from '../../../db/schema';"

expectations.text: Names the dependency rule violation explicitly — domain should have zero external dependencies
expectations.evidence: "In a properly layered architecture (Onion / Clean / Hexagonal), the domain layer must have zero knowledge of how data is persisted. It should define interfaces (ports) that infrastructure implementations fulfill."

expectations.text: Suggests introducing a repository interface in the domain layer
expectations.evidence: Fix section shows: "// domain/INotificationRepository.ts\nexport interface INotificationRepository { findUnreadByUser(userId: string): Promise<Notification[]>; ... }" and recommended structure includes 'INotificationRepository.ts # Port (interface)' under domain/

expectations.text: Suggests moving Drizzle logic to a separate repository/infrastructure file
expectations.evidence: Fix section shows: "// infrastructure/DrizzleNotificationRepository.ts\nimport { eq, and } from 'drizzle-orm'; ... export class DrizzleNotificationRepository implements INotificationRepository { // ... all Drizzle queries live here }"

expectations.text: Notes that routes.ts instantiates the service directly rather than using a composition root
expectations.evidence: Moderate Issue #3: 'Module-Level Singleton Service in Routes' — "NotificationService is instantiated as a module-level singleton with no way to inject dependencies (because the current implementation takes no constructor arguments)."
